newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Treasuries idle in London, look to debt sale.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries idle in London, look to debt sale.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries drifted in light London trade on Tuesday with little aside from the quarterly refunding later to latch on to.

Analysts said they expected scant reaction to the Treasury's sale of $17.0 billion of three-year paper later, but if anything, said the market may use the extra supply as an excuse to pare recent gains.
"The only focus is the quarterly refunding and even that won't move markets significantly," said Yamaichi international bond strategist Adam Chester.
"That might provide an excuse for a bit of downside. We've seen a strong move in Treasuries and the fact we do have supply may give dealers an excuse to mark prices down a bit."
The Treasury is also due to auction $12 billion of 10-year paper on Wednesday. Meanwhile, March factory orders will be released at 1400 GMT on Tuesday.

By 1135 GMT, the 30-year long bond was at 96-23, unchanged from Tokyo and 3/32 lower than the New York close. Three-year paper was at 98-23 versus 98-22 in Tokyo and 98-23 in New York and two-year paper was at 100-07, 1/32 down from Tokyo.
One dealer said there had been some demand for two-year paper.
The brokering of a deal on Friday to balance the U.S. budget by 2002 and last week's array of market-friendly economic data were bolstering the market, analysts said.
"Rightly or wrongly, the market is beginning to mark in no rate increase in May," said Adam Chester, U.S. economist at Yamaichi International in London.
"We're still looking for a move in May but it's by no means a done deal," he added.
Signs of GDP growth in the second quarter, of which Friday's favourable April jobs data were the first indicator, were crucial, Chester said.
